solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticise expert before a remedy for all is produced

indicators.note: before places the first pieces ahead of the following letter in the answer

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
an ace is an expert, someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: Someone rubbishes a specialist just before a universal cure turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all claimed to heal every ailment is the classic meaning of this word, from the Greek for all-healing.

clue.text: Swear after mate creates a fuss

indicators.note: after places the swearing word behind the friend

parts.note: a pal is a mate
to aver is to swear, declare

explanation.surface: Someone swearing at their friend causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaver is a tiresome to-do or commotion.

clue.text: Silky fabric and some linen in one

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cloth roll includes a soft fabric and a bit of linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightweight sheer fabric of silk or rayon, used for dresses.

clue.text: Stupid fool's after credit

indicators.note: after places the fool behind the credit letters

parts.note: ass means fool, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A fool chases credit he hasn't earned.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly stupid or insensitive.

clue.text: Social worker, girl, put up aerial

parts.note: an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

indicators.note: put up in a down clue reads the name from bottom to top

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A social worker and a young woman install a TV aerial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is a crossword favourite for an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an aerial for receiving signals.

clue.text: Place to set free skunk

indicators.note: setting the letters free lets them loose to form a new order

explanation.surface: A good spot to release a smelly animal into the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Polecat is a name used in North America for the skunk, another strong-smelling mammal.

clue.text: Moral tale raised in heel bar, apparently

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fable is told at a shoe-repair kiosk.
explanation.walkthrough: A heel bar is a British shoe-repair stall. 'in' points to the letters hidden inside the words; 'raised' in a down clue reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple story told to teach a moral lesson.

clue.text: French composer in row with philanderer

indicators.note: in places the composer inside the row

parts.note: a line is a row
Jacques Ibert was a French composer

explanation.surface: A French composer quarrels with a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a man who leads a dissolute, promiscuous life.

clue.text: Letter card

definitions.meaning: a letter of an alphabet or script
a card is an amusing eccentric person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a written symbol and an odd or amusing person.

clue.text: Rough terrain for a coach

indicators.note: rough means the letters are roughed up into disorder

explanation.surface: Bumpy ground is suited to a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a vehicle but is a person who trains athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer coaches people or animals in sport.

clue.text: House in historic city

definitions.meaning: a royal dynasty, the House that fought York in the Wars of the Roses
the county town of Lancashire, with its medieval castle

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an English royal dynasty and an old city in north-west England.

clue.text: Old master, pale and sickly, nursed by graduate

indicators.note: nursed by means held inside the graduate's letters like a child in arms

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
wan means pale and unwell-looking

explanation.surface: A former master, ill and pallid, is being looked after by someone with a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master' suggests a painting, but here it is a colonial-era form of address.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swahili term once used in East Africa to address a master or boss, now dated.

clue.text: Meat in oven's cooking

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are worked over into something new

parts.note: the 's is read as a letter S here

explanation.surface: Meat is being cooked in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer meat is the standard name for flesh from deer as food.

clue.text: Pub to do well out of deal

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to gain is to profit, to do well out of something

explanation.surface: The pub is set to profit from a business arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement between parties, especially a trade agreement, is a synonym of deal.

clue.text: One showing no principles about proving of will

parts.note: re means about, concerning
probate is the legal proving of a will

explanation.surface: An unscrupulous person is involved in proving a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel with no morals is described by this word for an unprincipled person.

clue.text: Girl and boy sign article

parts.note: Phil is a boy's name
an omen is a sign
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl and boy are given an ominous indication.
explanation.definitionFit: Philomena is a girl's name.

clue.text: Improving, continuously injecting them

indicators.note: injecting puts the following word into the middle

parts.note: on end means continuously, as in for hours on end

explanation.surface: Getting better after continuous injections.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering from illness or improving is expressed by this idiom.

clue.text: Bury at home against Exeter, losing first half

indicators.note: against means placed beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: losing first half means the opening three of the city's six letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Bury, playing at home, face Exeter and lose the first half.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a football fixture between Bury and Exeter City; 'Bury' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it in a grave.

clue.text: Riddle involving western author

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round the next piece

parts.note: to riddle is to sift through a sieve

explanation.surface: A puzzle concerning a cowboy-story writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but is a verb, to sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was the Anglo-Irish writer of Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Our bass relaxing in private

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Our bass singer unwinds away from the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for under the rose, an idiom for in secret or confidentially.

clue.text: Wired message, stuff about competent leader of group

indicators.note: about means going round the following pieces

parts.note: to cram is to stuff
able means competent

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of group

explanation.surface: A telegram stuffed with praise for a capable bandleader.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram sent by cable was a message transmitted along wires.

clue.text: Skipper in international leading reserves in

indicators.note: leading places the international ahead of the rest

parts.note: a cap is a player chosen for a national side, an international
TA, the Territorial Army, are reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A skipper in an international side leads his reserves onto the field.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain skippers a team or ship.

clue.text: Doorman, extremely bitter, carrying little weight

indicators.note: carrying means holding the weight inside
extremely takes the first and last letters of bitter

parts.note: an ounce is a small weight

explanation.surface: A doorman, very bitter, is not carrying much weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer guards the door of a club, keeping out troublemakers.

clue.text: Virtuoso and master playing ball

indicators.note: playing means the letters perform in a new order

parts.note: a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A virtuoso and his teacher are playing ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, a virtuoso performer.

clue.text: Audible cries of disapproval at college drinking session

indicators.note: audible says the word is to be heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: boos are cries of disapproval
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Students jeer during a drunken party at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A booze-up is informal slang for a session of heavy drinking.

clue.text: Put into employment, is seen in posh topper

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

indicators.note: seen in places the little word inside the hat

parts.note: a tile is slang for a hat, a topper

explanation.surface: Someone put to work wears a fancy top hat.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE is dated British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To utilise is to make use of, to put something to work.

clue.text: A side changed plans

indicators.note: changed means the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A team was altered and so were the tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are plans or schemes in the mind.

clue.text: I spot one inside supplying dope

indicators.note: inside places the numeral within the spot

parts.note: a dot is a spot
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone notices an insider supplying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person.

clue.text: Corpulent old boy seen mostly in disarray

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: in disarray means the remaining letters are jumbled
mostly drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: the word taken as written

explanation.surface: A fat old boy is seen looking dishevelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SEEN to SEE; 'in disarray' scrambles that to ESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very fat, a synonym of corpulent.

clue.text: Child, in transforming metal, is a budding scientist

indicators.note: in places the child's letters inside the rearranged ones
transforming means the letters change shape

explanation.surface: A child turning metals into something else must be a young scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link verb but is part of the fodder that 'transforming' scrambles into ALEMIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval practitioners trying to transmute metals were forerunners of chemistry, hence early or budding scientists.

clue.text: A group working in desert

parts.note: a band is a group
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A band playing in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a sandy place but is a verb, to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone is to leave them behind for good.

clue.text: Dish male teacher rejected — too much duck!

indicators.note: rejected turns the letters back the other way

parts.note: sir is how pupils address a male teacher
OTT, over the top, means too much
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A teacher refuses a meal, saying there is far too much duck in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.
